message: delivery-scope.jsonl clause GROUP-COMMIT-BYTE-GATE-7 still describes StorageLimits::DEFAULT.max_journal_batch_bytes as defaulting to 1_048_576 (payload basis, matching the State 2 open question). The resolved contract value per contract.md §6 M-HN4SC-9 is 1_048_636 (encoded basis, = 60 + 1_048_576), which is what the proof-strategy.md, domain-model.md, type-contracts.md, and proof-coverage-matrix.md all use. The plan correctly uses 1_048_636 throughout and the const-assertion obligation POB-vb-hn4sc-003 enforces the corrected binding at compile time, so the runtime will be correct. The drift is a documentation inconsistency in the planning scope only.
required_fix: No runtime fix required. Optional: update delivery-scope.jsonl GROUP-COMMIT-BYTE-GATE-7 text to 1_048_636 (encoded basis) and reference the resolved M-HN4SC-9 hazard for traceability. The proof plan itself is internally consistent.
approval_ref: contract.md §6 M-HN4SC-9 (Important correction from the draft hazard analysis)
rationale: The State 3 rust-contract has already resolved the GROUP-COMMIT-BYTE-GATE-7 open question by choosing option (b) DEFAULT_JOURNAL_BATCH_BYTES_INCLUSIVE_OF_HEADER = 1_048_636, and the State 4 proof plan applies that resolution. The const-assertion obligation POB-vb-hn4sc-003 binds the storage default to the encoded-basis constant at compile time, so a future drift would fail cargo check -p vb_storage with E0080. Updating delivery-scope.jsonl is documentation hygiene, not a correctness fix; it does not block plan approval.

message: proof-strategy.md §7 and proof-coverage-matrix.md POB-vb-hn4sc-003 reference crate::storage_constants::DEFAULT_JOURNAL_BATCH_BYTES_INCLUSIVE_OF_HEADER, but the module file crates/vb_storage/src/storage_constants.rs does not yet exist (verified absent on disk). The const-assertion block cannot compile without the alias, so the obligation implicitly requires creating the module file. This is a legitimate implementation-time scope add, but it is referenced as a binding site without an explicit obligation tracking its creation.
required_fix: No plan fix required. The proof-to-implementation bridge at State 7 must record crates/vb_storage/src/storage_constants.rs as a new production file in the bridge rows for POB-vb-hn4sc-003. The implementation at State 11 must add the new module before the const-assertion compiles. The proof-writer at State 5 does not need to touch the new module.
rationale: The new module is a single pub const alias with no behavioral surface; the const-assertion contract implicitly demands its existence. Tracking it as a separate obligation would add bureaucratic noise. The proof-to-implementation bridge will note the new file in the source_refs and the formal-verifier at State 12 will catch a missing file at compile time.

message: POB-vb-hn4sc-002 (proptest length roundtrip) claims proptest 1.11.0 compatibility via single-test form. The existing proptest_storage.rs (vb-b8i8f LANDING-NOTE-001) is disabled because of block-form incompatibility, but proptests.rs (lib.rs:122-124) and po010_proptests.rs (lib.rs:108-110) are wired and use the supported single-test form. The plan's compatibility claim is consistent with the wired modules. The exact proptest dependency version should be confirmed by the formal-verifier at State 12 before running the evidence command.
required_fix: No plan fix required. The formal-verifier at State 12 will pin proptest to the version declared in Cargo.toml and run `cargo test --lib -p vb_storage --features proptest queue::tests::length_roundtrip` to produce the raw evidence log. The plan's proptest_version: "1.11.0" field is a guidance hint, not a constraint.
rationale: proptest 1.11.0 single-test form is the supported pattern in the existing wired modules. The plan's compatibility claim is verified against the existing wiring. The formal-verifier at State 12 will produce the actual raw log with the pinned version, so the plan does not need to over-specify.
